solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Language making fellow bishop defect

indicators.note: 'making X Y' tells us one thing is turned into another, so one letter is swapped for a different one

blocks.note: Flemish is the Dutch spoken in Belgium
F is the abbreviation for fellow
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman deserts his flock, and a language is somehow involved in his treachery.
explanation.walkthrough: The F of FLEMISH is replaced by B. 'Defect' reads as a verb about a bishop switching sides, but it is the noun meaning a flaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A blemish is a flaw or imperfection, the same sense as the noun defect.

clue.text: Snake nurses caught in capital

indicators.note: to nurse something is to hold it close, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a boa is a large constricting snake
to have got someone is to have caught them

explanation.surface: A snake holds nurses trapped somewhere in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogota is the capital city of Colombia.

clue.text: Choose key at end of bar for conductor

indicators.note: placing one item at the end of another fixes their order when they are joined

blocks.note: to elect is to choose
a rod is a bar
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Advice to pick a musical key that suits the end of a bar, for an orchestra's conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical surface makes 'conductor' a person with a baton; here it means a component that carries electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a terminal through which electricity enters or leaves, i.e. an electrical conductor.

clue.text: Problem with venue Saskia regularly brought up

indicators.note: regularly means at steady intervals, so every other letter of the words is taken
in a down clue, bringing something up reads it from bottom to top

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Someone named Saskia raises a complaint about the venue.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a matter in dispute or a problem to be dealt with.

clue.text: Male pony maybe drinking writer's weedkiller

indicators.note: something drinking takes another thing inside it

blocks.note: he is the male pronoun
a pony is an example of something to ride
a Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen, a writer; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A stallion pony is drinking someone's weedkiller, a worrying farmyard accident.
explanation.walkthrough: A pony is something you ride, so 'pony maybe' gives the activity; Bic is a well-known make of ballpoint, a writing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbicide is a chemical used to destroy unwanted plants, which is what a weedkiller is.

clue.text: Leaves sailor in bed, returning with company

indicators.note: one thing being in another places it inside
returning means going back, so the combined letters are read backwards
with simply adds the next piece alongside

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A sailor in his bunk heads back home with his shipmates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb about the sailor departing, but it is the plural noun for cured plant leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco is sold as the dried, cured leaves of the tobacco plant.

clue.text: Very warm cycling with new German underwear

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round in a loop, so the first letter goes to the back

blocks.note: very warm is hot
N is the abbreviation for new
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A cyclist on a hot day wears new German underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: HOT is cycled so its final T moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a skimpy item of underwear with a narrow strip at the back.

clue.text: Primitive dig on area over in Russia

indicators.note: one letter placed in a word goes inside it

blocks.note: a dig is a cutting remark, a barb
A is the abbreviation for area
RUS is an abbreviation for Russia
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A primitive archaeological dig on a site abroad in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig' suggests excavation, but it is a jibe; 'over' is the cricket term for six balls, abbreviated O.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbarous means uncivilised or primitive.

clue.text: Obsessive follows college course in Amsterdam?

indicators.note: follows puts one piece after the other in the joined answer

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for college
anal is slang for obsessively fussy

explanation.surface: An obsessive student takes a college course while studying in Amsterdam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' sounds academic, but it is a watercourse; Amsterdam is famous for them, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Amsterdam is crossed by many canals, man-made waterways along which water takes its course.

clue.text: Exaggerate merits of old poetry before local emptied

indicators.note: before places the earlier pieces ahead of the last one
emptying a word removes its inside, leaving only the outer letters

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
verse is poetry
only the first and last letters remain

explanation.surface: Someone overpraises old poetry before the village pub has emptied out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British slang for a neighbourhood pub, which helps the surface; here it just supplies two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversell something is to praise or promote it more than it deserves.

clue.text: Visitors ignoring temperature estimate

indicators.note: ignoring a thing leaves it out, so one letter is dropped

blocks.note: visitors are guests
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: Visitors pay no heed to the thermometer and estimate how warm it is.
explanation.walkthrough: One T is removed from GUESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A guess is a rough estimate made without full information.

clue.text: Eastern ring road confused long-distance runner

indicators.note: something confused is muddled, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
taken as written

explanation.surface: A marathon runner gets lost on an eastern ring road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but a river is a crossword runner, and the Rio Grande is a very long one.
explanation.definitionFit: Rivers run, and the Rio Grande flows nearly 2,000 miles along the US–Mexico border.

clue.text: Little one by sides of the arena about to fall?

indicators.note: by means beside, so the pieces are set next to each other
the sides of a word are its two edge letters

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
first and last letters
a ring is an arena, as for boxing or the circus

explanation.surface: A toddler wobbling about beside a circus ring looks ready to topple.
explanation.definitionFit: Tottering means walking unsteadily, as if on the point of falling; the question mark admits it is a loose gloss.

clue.text: Book of charts finally stolen at the end

indicators.note: something stolen is taken away, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: the final letter of the phrase is what goes
at last means at the end

explanation.surface: A book of maps finally got stolen when all was over.
explanation.walkthrough: AT LAST loses its final letter, the one 'finally stolen' points at.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound collection of maps, i.e. a book of charts.

clue.text: Scheming inmate given pairs tailor fabricated

indicators.note: fabricated means made up or constructed, so the letters are assembled into a new order

blocks.note: con is slang for a convict
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prisoner given a couple of tailors makes a plotting deal in the workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: Conspiratorial describes someone plotting in secret, which is what scheming means.

clue.text: US student awfully morose eating noodle soup

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters are rearranged
eating takes something inside

blocks.note: taken as written
pho is a Vietnamese noodle soup

explanation.surface: A gloomy American student sits eating a bowl of noodle soup.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a sophomore is a student in the second year of high school or college.

clue.text: Lacking faith in theft after a time, I see

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other when they are joined

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
a heist is a robbery
taken as written
C is a letter pronounced like 'see'

explanation.surface: Someone notices, after a while, a lack of faith in the robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheistic describes a person who does not believe in God, i.e. lacking religious faith.

clue.text: Shifting realities for Jacob's descendant

indicators.note: shifting means moving around, so the letters change their positions

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Changing times bring new realities for the descendants of Jacob.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob was renamed Israel in Genesis, so his descendants, the twelve tribes, are Israelites.

clue.text: Lily's snake died in pit with tail twisted

indicators.note: twisting the tail of a word jumbles only its end letters, leaving the rest in order
a letter in a word goes inside it

blocks.note: an asp is a venomous snake
a pit is a hole
D is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A lily's resident snake died in a pit with its tail twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: The last two letters of HOLE, its tail, are swapped, then D goes in to make HODEL. The 's means 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a plant of the lily family, linked in Greek myth with the underworld.

clue.text: Delight overwhelms child amid cattle and racing horses

indicators.note: to overwhelm something is to engulf it, so it ends up inside
amid means in the middle of

blocks.note: steers are young castrated bulls
to delight is to please
CH is the abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: A child is thrilled to be among cattle and racehorses on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the child sits inside the delight, and that whole unit sits inside the cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Steeplechasers are horses that race over fences and ditches in a steeplechase.

clue.text: Allow instruction perhaps to hair stylist

blocks.note: first meaning: to let something happen
second meaning, split in two: an order to give someone's hair a perm

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as PERM IT, what you might tell a hairdresser.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit is to allow, and a perm is a chemical curling treatment for hair.

clue.text: Animal cool next to river

indicators.note: next to sets the two pieces side by side

blocks.note: hip is slang for fashionable or cool
the Po is the longest river in Italy

explanation.surface: A trendy creature lounging beside the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A hippo, short for hippopotamus, is a large African animal that lives near rivers.

clue.text: Bone held by a painter's subject?

indicators.note: something held by another is enclosed in it

blocks.note: per means 'a', as in so much per hour
os is Latin and anatomical for bone

explanation.surface: An artist's model holds a bone as a prop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' as in 'twice a day' means per.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is someone who poses, as an artist's model does; the question mark marks the loose sense.

clue.text: Some Charlie let Neil call back customers

indicators.note: some means only part of the words, so the letters lie within them
back means the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the end of Charlie, then let, Neil and the start of call

explanation.surface: Charlie allows Neil to ring the customers back.
explanation.definitionFit: A business's clientele is its body of clients, its customers taken together.

clue.text: Tough cut in vacant carvery

indicators.note: vacant means empty, so the inside letters go and the outer ones stay
a piece placed in another goes inside it

blocks.note: first and last letters
to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: A tough slice of meat in an empty carvery restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: A carvery is a British restaurant serving roast meat carved to order.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewy food, like tough meat, needs a lot of chewing.

clue.text: Note female bird raised in country

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising letters reads them upwards, in reverse

blocks.note: la is a note of the sol-fa scale
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A note about a female bird reared in some country.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a country in the Himalayas between India and China.

clue.text: Corrupt officer excelled ultimately as sergeant

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each word

blocks.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, a police officer
to shine at something is to excel
the last letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A bent police officer who performed best of all as a sergeant.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrupt and dishonest both describe someone acting fraudulently for gain.

clue.text: Stiffly formal embracing adult Homeric king

indicators.note: embracing something wraps around it, so it sits inside

blocks.note: prim means stiffly proper
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A starchy figure clasping a grown-up, a king out of Homer.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam was King of Troy during the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Turned all grey for the most part

indicators.note: turned suggests being changed or twisted about, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's hair went entirely grey, or at least mostly.
explanation.definitionFit: Largely means mainly, to a great extent, which is what 'for the most part' says.

clue.text: Fetch bowed object from the rear inside court

indicators.note: reading from the rear means starting at the end and going backwards
inside places one piece within another

blocks.note: CT is the abbreviation for court
a cello is played with a bow

explanation.surface: Fetch a bent object from the back of the courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowed' suggests bent over, but here it means played with a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: To collect someone or something is to go and fetch it.
